purpose: Defines what an error is, how to classify it, and how to treat causes, plus criteria for adding values that distinguish errors, applicable to exit codes, agent return values, error cases, and API codes.
summary: Purpose: stop unbounded growth of error values that do not change receiver behavior
Definition of an error as an event where processing departs from the intended flow
Judgeable outcomes are not errors and should be decided first
Classification into recoverable and unrecoverable (fatal) errors
Recovery means are not always retries; unrecoverable errors stop and report
Causes: bug, failure, user input or environment, with responsible parties
Bugs must not occur at runtime and get no dedicated values or recovery paths
Questions to ask before adding an error value
tasks: Designing error handling for scripts or agents
Adding exit codes or return values that distinguish errors
Writing error case sections in requirements documents
Reviewing code or documents for error handling violations
Deciding whether a failure should be an error or a judgment
title: エラーの定義・分類・原因
